Application Materials.content:
- A **500-word personal statement** should include your reasons for choosing the course, the modules/areas of study you are particularly interested in, the skills and knowledge you are hoping to gain, and a demonstration of your relevant skills and experience.
- You’ll need to upload certain documents as part of the application process, including:
- Transcripts of your qualifications
- English language test certificates if taken
- Personal statement (if not written directly into the portal)
- Scholarship documentation (if applying)
- Don’t worry if you don’t have all of your documents with you when you apply as you can always upload them later through the portal.

Application Deadlines.content: In most cases, applications for postgraduate courses can be made **at any time in the year**, provided that you allow enough time for a decision to be made on your application and for you to make any necessary arrangements, such as visa applications if applicable. Some courses may close early if there is high demand for places, so check the programme information for details. Postgraduate taught programmes start in **late September**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- We require a **2:1 Bachelor (Honours) degree or international equivalent in any degree subject**.
- The Master of Data Science (Social Analytics) is a conversion course that opens up a future in data science, **even if your first degree is in a non-quantitative subject** (including the social sciences, the arts and humanities).
- Applicants with a strong data science or mathematical background may wish to consider the MSc Scientific Computing and Data Analysis programmes.
- **China applicants:** A standard full-time bachelor’s degree (**4 years minimum**), with a minimum average grade of between **75% - 85%** from a recognised prestigious university. Applicants from non-prestigious institution with a minimum grade of **90% or above** will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Program Overview.content:
The Master of Data Science (Social Analytics) at Durham University equips you with the tools to analyse complex social data, uncover patterns in human behaviour, and inform evidence-based decision-making. Whether you're aiming for a career in government, policy, market research, or social impact organisations, this programme prepares you to lead with insight in a data-driven world.
- Start date: September 2026
- Degree type: MDS
- Course code: G5P423
- Course length: 1 year full-time
Use data to understand and improve society. This conversion course equips you with the skills to analyse social data, uncover patterns in human behaviour, and inform policy and business decisions. Learn to apply advanced data science techniques to real-world social challenges across sectors.
The Master of Data Science (Social Analytics) is a conversion course that opens up a future in data science, even if your first degree is in a non-quantitative subject (including the social sciences, the arts and humanities). The course equips you with the skills to process and analyse data, communicate your findings to a wide audience, whilst applying this knowledge to practical situations.
The MDS provides training in contemporary data science, learning from practising researchers who are making a difference across a range of industries. Shared core modules across the suite of MDS courses build wider skills in statistical and machine learning, while subject-specific modules integrate data science with social science, equipping you with the skills to design and carry out social data science research and communicate it to optimise impact across a variety of settings.
The MDS culminates in the research project, an in-depth investigation into an area of specific interest in which you apply the skills learned during the course to a research problem in a social science domain of your choice. The Durham Research Methods Centre can help with the allocation of project topics through local authorities, NHS Trusts and the wider health and social care sector.
The course begins with a range of introductory modules before progressing to more advanced contemporary techniques such as statistical modelling (in R), computer programming (in Python), machine learning, AI and neural networks. Social analytics modules provide insight into the specialised methods needed for social data as well as the theoretical foundations to understand how to use them effectively.
This interdisciplinary course is made up of modules that span across the University. It incorporates a wide range of learning and teaching methods, including lectures, seminars, workshops and computer/practical classes. The taught elements are further reinforced through independent study, research and analysis, case studies and structured reading. All modules are underpinned by research and embed elements of research training in both delivery and assessment.
The Master of Data Science is assessed via a combination of essays, online assessments, reports and presentations – both individual and in small groups. The course culminates with a major research project, which is conducted and written up as a self-directed piece of work with support from your appointed supervisor.
Data Science is a conversion course that incorporates content from many Departments across the University. This provides access to a selection of related modern facilities from across the University, in particular Computer Science and Mathematics. Facilities will depend on the subject specialism but include laboratories, libraries, project spaces, lecture theatres, study and networking spaces as well as shared social spaces. Most departments are close to the historic centre of Durham which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
In today’s data-driven world, the ability to capture, analyse, and communicate insights from complex information is one of the most sought-after skills by employers globally. Graduates are equipped for exciting and meaningful careers across a wide range of sectors, from science, health, and the environment to the humanities and social policy, where data is driving innovation and transforming how we live and work.

Curriculum.content:
Course length: 1 year full-time.
The course begins with a range of introductory modules before progressing to more advanced contemporary techniques such as statistical modelling (in R), computer programming (in Python), machine learning, AI and neural networks. Social analytics modules provide insight into the specialised methods needed for social data as well as the theoretical foundations to understand how to use them effectively.
Core modules:
- The Data Science Research Project is a substantial piece of self directed research into an unfamiliar area of data science, or in your subject specialisation area with a focus on data science. The project can be practical, theoretical or both, and is designed to develop your research, analysis and report-writing skills.
- Critical Perspectives in Data Science and AI develops your understanding of the production, analysis and use of quantified data, and how to analyse these practices anthropologically utilising AI applications.
- Causal Inference introduces causal inference frameworks and research design techniques used to explore causation in social science.
- Full Stack Research Design teaches the full research design process in the social sciences, from crafting research questions to selecting data and methods, and communicating findings to diverse audiences.
- Programming for Data Science uses popular Python software packages used in a wide range of industry settings.
- Introduction to Statistics for Data Science covers exploratory statistics, statistical inference; linear models; classification and clustering methods; and resampling and validation.
Optional modules: The remainder of the course will be made up of core and option modules which will vary depending on prior qualifications and experience. Example optional modules have previously included:
- Introduction to Computer Science
- Introduction to Mathematics for Data Science
- Text Mining and Language Analytics
- Data Exploration, Visualisation and Unsupervised Learning
- Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science
- Strategic Leadership
- Machine Learning
- Computational Social Science

Financial Aid.content:
The **Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship** is available to all new international students to Durham who meet the eligibility criteria. Each scholarship is a competitive award worth up to **£10,000** in tuition fee discounts towards the original tuition fee for a postgraduate programme starting in **September 2026**.
| Field | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Amount | The scholarship is offered in two award types: **Inspiring Excellence £5K** - £5,000 in tuition fee discount; **Inspiring Excellence £10K** - £10,000 in tuition fee discount |
| Year of Entry | Scholarships are available for programmes commencing in 2026. |
| Number of awards available | Limited |
| Level of study | Postgraduate Taught |
| Eligible programmes | One-year, full-time (in-person) taught MSc, MA, LLM or MDS qualification (MBA, MSW programmes and MA in Theology and Ministry are excluded). |
| Duration | One-year |
To be eligible, applicants must:
- have applied to a one-year, full-time (in-person) taught MSc, MA, LLM or MDS qualification (MBA, MSW programmes and MA in Theology and Ministry are excluded).
- start postgraduate studies at Durham University in **September 2026**.
- be classed as an overseas student for fee-paying purposes.
- self-funded and not already in receipt of any other scholarship, funding or sponsorship.
- meet or exceed the entry requirements for the programme applied for at Durham University.
- complete the [Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship Application Form](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fforms.office.com%2FPages%2FResponsePage.aspx%3Fid%3Di9hQcmhLKUW-RNWaLYpvlF0WV-CJxblAsFZLqIzpDTZUQU4xSFo1WUdIVzhOT044V1hYWEJMUEFYQi4u&data=05%7C02%7Cbethea.etherington%40durham.ac.uk%7C130312b9ee024d43c26b08ddff49a6ac%7C7250d88b4b684529be44d59a2d8a6f94%7C0%7C0%7C638947413974172128%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=mV6BXieSd608vvbHSUHl8EDk%2B8MqYE%2FPZ%2BbGqickNpY%3D&reserved=0).
To apply, applicants must first apply for an eligible postgraduate programme via Durham's [Postgraduate Applicant Portal](https://studyatdurham.microsoftcrmportals.com/en-US/), then submit the scholarship application form by: 1st round selection: midnight (GMT) **16January 2026**; Additional round selection: midnight (GMT) **20 March 2026**; 2nd round selection: midnight (GMT) **29 May 2026**. If an applicant fails to receive an academic offer before the deadline for the 1st round selection, or is unsuccessful in the 1st round selection, they will be automatically considered for the next round selection and **do not need to submit the scholarship application form again**.
The Durham Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship applies to courses commencing in September 2026. The scholarship award is not transferable, not deferrable and will be applied as a tuition fee waiver directly to the postgraduate programme tuition fees. No cash alternative is offered. The tuition fees will be adjusted at the time of enrolment at Durham University. Awardees will lose eligibility for the award if they are no longer classified as overseas students for fee purposes, or receive other scholarships, funding, or sponsorship from Durham or external institutions during their degree.

Multiple Applications.content: You can apply for as many Masters Programmes as you choose. Applicants can receive two or more offers, but can accept only one. Once an offer is accepted, any other applications will be automatically declined.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
We’re able to consider, on a case-by-case basis:
- Change of year
- Change of course
- Change of mode of study.
You can request a change through your Applicant Portal homepage. We aren’t able to approve all requests, but if we are able to you will receive a new offer letter which you will be able to view in your Applicant Portal. If you request a deferral your application will be deferred and reconsidered when the next admissions cycle opens. You can only defer **one year at a time** (for example from 2026 to 2027 - not 2028). If you are unable to take up your place following a deferral, you will need to submit a new application in the next cycle.
